title: The Pillar and the Womb
english: They say the law: 'You shall not make for yourself a pillar' (Exodus 20:4), signifying that everyone who practices forbidden things raises up a life like a pillar. Therefore, one may also rightly say that the one doing good things is setting up a pillar, as a symbol of the contests through which he has struggled.

For such is the fruit of righteousness (Psalm 57:3), and in Proverbs: 'To perceive true justice and to direct judgment' (Proverbs 21:15). But injustice entangles, joining sin by acting without distinction in evil. This is equal to the binding of one's own sins in a knot. It is not in vain that you work iniquity in the land (Jeremiah 23:24); for if someone makes iniquity in the heart, he works it in the land, that is, concerning material things.

Those daring to slander the Scriptures and dragging this word into error, saying that those who are led astray from the stomach and speak lies are not [true], say that the fulfillment of the word is sinning. It is not right to say that those who have not perceived the habit of the Scripture have thought these things; the newborn infant is receptive to virtue and to wickedness in power, then receiving by operation whichever of these two it encounters, it will know good and evil. For then also the word is fulfilled, when it begins to act according to virtue. It is said that the good has been made from the mother's womb. Such is what Job says: 'Even if I ate my morsel alone and did not share with the orphan' (Job 31:32); for from the mother's womb they guided them and I nourished them as a father. And those who, failing regarding the word, rushed to the fulfillment of the word from error, began to act. And the expression 'to speak' signifies 'having spoken lies.' Perhaps also, as in the preceding verse, to be a shepherd and to be of another birth: those born from a bad teaching, from the very stomach that bore them, [referring to] the being led astray and the speaking of lies.

They say that the ears of an ox, the so-called 'palms,' are carrying a shield. For if ever a singer, according to his own wisdom, were able to carry a song capable of lulling it to sleep, if it were to hear, the ox would lay its ears upon the non-hearing of the singer's voice, as if a medicine being prepared by a wise man. And they also lay [their ears], not the ears of sensation but the ears of intellect, so that they might not hear the wise songs being proclaimed...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Deliverance from Lawless Workers
english: Death of life. He does not rejoice exultantly, but, lest he himself be subject to punishment, he purifies his own deeds, becoming more secure (Ps 57:11a).

When one Saul is pursuing him, he prays to be rescued from many enemies (Ps 58:2-3). He prays not to be [rescued] from the spear-bearers sleeping with Saul, or from the predatory demons acting against him, saying 'many enemies' to be rescued from them. And he prays to be liberated from these rising up against him, wishing perhaps that the ransom of the one being liberated might be to give his own soul instead of many.

But workers of lawlessness are those doing what the law forbids, and since among the forbidden things is murder, men are men of blood, preferring to kill men because of the coming brutishness. But he who is not bothered by those working lawlessness is rescued, being under the protection of God, and also he who is not handed over into the hands of those willing to shed his blood is saved from murderous men.

And in another way: one is rescued from these; for he who does not work lawlessness but is disposed contrary to those doing it is rescued from the disposition of practical lawless acts, just as he who exists outside of murderous intent is saved, not being associated with murderous men.

The verses are to be interpreted thus: since men commit the work of lawlessness while the devil and his angels are working in men, he prays to be rescued from the devil and those with him who precede in the work of lawlessness. The testimony of this thought is: from the beginning the devil sins. For following that, others fall into sin in whom he works. Having cast betrayal into the heart of Judas, he became a traitor, following the thought of betrayal because of the one who incited him to this.

And also to add 'men' to the murderers; for it is not by chance, but the blood of a man is poured out by one strong and perfect in evils. Regarding the intention and brutishness of Saul and those sent by him to take him from his own people and to kill him (Ps 58:4a), he says, 'They have sought my soul, though by the power of God I shall be saved,' by a paradoxical art.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Discipline and Repentance
english: He is Lord, the God of the divine powers, but also the God of Israel, attending to visit the nations so that He might heal them as they are being badly consumed by idolatry and the service of demons. The visitation of the nations occurs because the divine Word has been sent to heal all and to save them from the corruptions that take hold beforehand. Indeed, He is a physician of souls, healing those who are crushed in heart. He is called God of powers and Lord of the rational, holy animals and heavenly hosts. Just as He is God of these powers, so also, by the voice of the discerning men called Hebrews of Israel, He is God (Ps 58:10-11).

While David was being pursued by Saul because of the aforementioned envy, he knew what the successor of the kingdom would be. And having prophetically seen what was to come, and having been anointed for this by Samuel—though he was not yet fully filled with the knowledge of it—he did not repeatedly rush into his hands, wanting to legally receive the kingdom from God, but not to seize it by assault and murder. From this intention he says, 'God is my strength, I will guard myself toward You' (Ps 58:10), not intending to strike, but waiting to receive it from You; and I am confident in this assurance, having known through experience many times that You are both God and my perceiver. For it is not by our power that we are worthy to reign, but rather Your mercy, having foretold me, will show itself to me among my enemies, in which they shall be disciplined by falling under punishment, but I shall receive the kingdom from You.

And regarding the thought of reigning from God according to Abraham: it is written that if some say to the patriarch while he is not perceptibly ruling, 'King, You are with us,' ruling pleasingly to God, he says, 'My God is my strength, I will guard myself toward You' (Ps 58:12); for You will lead into the kingdom those who have spoken, as the Corinthians say, 'And it would be good if you reigned, that we might reign with you.' (Ps 58:13ab). As a matter of history: the enemies lying in wait are worthy to be rebuked by God, but not to die. For it is not right that, if they remained wicked, they should die, for they would bring an end to the divine law; but being scattered by the power of God and being handed over to captivity, they will cry out to...

Having experienced God as a trial of punishment. But He also wills that they be brought low from the height of the pride they possess, which is the one defending the Lord who carries up the prayer. For complete punishment prepares and turns [one] toward recognition. But David, sparing them from this, pleaded that they might be disciplined by a more moderate punishment so that they might be sober; he adds the following: for if they are scattered, they are punished at once, and they will be able to be gathered together again having repented. Likewise, He also wills that they be brought low, that is, humbled: [to stop] the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips, which is beneficial both to those being humbled and to the majority, so that they may not be provoked to zeal against those speaking and saying things in pride and unrighteousness. For those having spoken with pride, having lied against the righteous, receiving the condemnation in the pride of their own words contrary to their works, they receive [it] as if being caught as lawless men being reproved.

It is to be reproved also from the present word those who think with a defensive mindset that the Creator is a heretic (Ps 59:3). God is angry not to destroy, but to have mercy. By this, 'I will bless You, Lord, what You were angry with me for, toward salvation' (Ps 59:3). For if He is angry toward salvation and toward mercy, His anger is not a passion, but is received usefully.

Those striving for material things and thinking of earthly things (Ps 59:4), regarding them as being stable and imperturbable, this such a state brings harm to them; it is better to be shaken and troubled by the mercy of God in a useful way. For having known that to be entangled in material things and to think of them causes trouble and shaking, turning away from the former bad life toward a serious [one], without care and having been crushed, having received the realization of the existing destructions from the demons, she will call upon the Lord who is able to heal these things.

Hard things are shown to someone if he falls into painful [circumstances] (Ps 59:5); but if anyone receives [them] toward the recognition of former sins, he drinks the wine of compunction, taking from the drinking the cause of being moved to repentance. Often the Scripture unreservedly calls the hard circumstances 'hard things'.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
